clauses.text: CNB Amanah Berhad (Registration No. 202101002895 (1403193-P)) (“CNB”, “we” or “us”) is a trust company registered under the Trust Companies Act 1949. We are the data user responsible for your personal data under the Personal Data Protection Act 2010 (“PDPA”).

This notice explains how we collect, use, disclose and protect personal data in connection with our trust products marketed as MyTrustbyCNB (“MyTrust”), our trust management system known as TheTrust (the “Portal”) and our websites at cnbamanah.com, thetrust.my and thewill.my (the “Websites”).

It applies to you if you are a settlor, beneficiary, caretaker, witness, joint account holder or authorised person in relation to a trust; a trust representative or advisor appointed by us (whether holding a V code or a W code) or a person acting for an agency appointed by us; or a visitor to the Websites or user of the Portal.
This notice is issued in English and Bahasa Malaysia. If there is any inconsistency between the two versions, the English version prevails.
Depending on your relationship with us, we may collect the following categories of personal data:
Identity data — name, NRIC, passport number or company registration number, date of birth, nationality, gender, and a copy or image of your identity document;
Contact data — residential and correspondence address, telephone number and email address;
Financial data — bank account details for payout or distribution, source of funds and source of wealth, payment slips and transaction records;
Trust data — your relationship to the settlor or beneficiaries, distribution wishes, payment purposes and frequency, caretaker details and the contents of your trust documents;
Tax data — tax residency, tax identification number and self-certifications required under FATCA and the Common Reporting Standard;
Representative data — agent code, introducer or upline, rank, personal sales and commission records, bank details, training and assessment records and declarations given at onboarding;
Technical data — login identifier, IP address, device and browser information, session tokens, cookies and audit logs of actions taken in the Portal; and

Sensitive personal data — health information, only where a distribution under a trust is conditional on total and permanent disability or medical care; and bankruptcy and criminal record screening results for trust representatives. We obtain your explicit consent separately before processing sensitive personal data.
We collect personal data:
directly from you, when you complete our forms, including the KYC Form, Instruction Form, Letter of Wishes and Trust Deed, or communicate with us;
through our appointed trust representatives, who collect it from you on our behalf;
through the Portal and the Websites when you register, log in or submit information;

from third parties, including screening and sanctions databases, the Companies Commission of Malaysia, the Malaysian Department of Insolvency, banks, and Ascent Capital Private Equity Sdn Bhd (“Ascent Capital”) as manager of the fund in which trust assets are placed; and
from publicly available sources.
We process personal data for the following purposes:
to assess your application and establish a trust with us;

to verify your identity and carry out know-your-customer and customer due diligence checks, sanctions screening and reporting required under the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001, FATCA and the Common Reporting Standard;
to prepare, execute, stamp and administer your trust documents;
to receive, hold and release trust assets, including placing them with Ascent CNB PLT or any other fund managed by Ascent Capital, and to receive reports on those assets;
to make distributions and payments to beneficiaries and caretakers in accordance with the trust;
to communicate with you about your trust, your account or your appointment;
to appoint, train, rank and pay trust representatives, including computing personal and overriding commission;
to operate, secure, maintain and improve the Portal and the Websites;
to keep statutory, accounting and audit records and to report to regulators;
to handle enquiries, complaints and disputes, and to establish, exercise or defend legal claims; and

with your consent, to inform you about CNB’s own trust and legacy planning products. You may opt out at any time by writing to us at the address in Section 15, and we will stop within a reasonable time.

title: WHO WE SHARE PERSONAL DATA WITH

clauses.text: We may disclose personal data, to the extent necessary for the purposes above, to:
Ascent Capital and Ascent CNB PLT, for the placement, management and reporting of trust assets;
Lee & Partners Trustees Berhad and companies within the Lee & Partners group that are involved in trust administration;
our appointed trust representatives and agencies, limited to the trust cases they introduced;
our system developer and hosting or cloud service providers, who process data on our behalf under written contracts;
couriers, banks, stamping agents, auditors, solicitors and tax agents;

the Securities Commission Malaysia, Bank Negara Malaysia, the Inland Revenue Board of Malaysia, the Malaysian Department of Insolvency, the courts and any other regulator or authority where required by law or on lawful request; and
any person who acquires, or proposes to acquire, all or part of our business.
We do not sell personal data.

Personal data is stored on servers located in Malaysia and our appointed cloud service providers may operate back-up or support nodes outside Malaysia. Where we transfer personal data outside Malaysia, we do so only as permitted under section 129 of the PDPA and with contractual safeguards that require the recipient to protect the data to a standard no lower than that required under Malaysian law.

We apply role-based access controls so that staff and representatives see only the records their role requires, encrypt data in transit, keep audit logs of actions taken in the Portal, review access rights periodically, and require our staff, representatives and service providers to sign confidentiality undertakings.
No transmission over the internet is completely secure. You should keep your login details confidential and tell us immediately if you suspect unauthorised access to your account.

title: HOW LONG WE KEEP PERSONAL DATA

clauses.text: We keep personal data relating to a trust for as long as the trust subsists and for seven (7) years after it ends, or for any longer period required by the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 or the applicable limitation period.
Personal data in applications that are rejected or withdrawn is kept for seven (7) years from the date of rejection or withdrawal. Portal audit logs are kept for twenty-four (24) months.
When personal data is no longer required, we delete it or anonymise it.
Under the PDPA you have the right to:
request access to the personal data we hold about you. We may charge the prescribed fee and will respond within twenty-one (21) days of receiving a complete request;
request correction of personal data that is inaccurate, incomplete, misleading or out of date;

withdraw your consent to processing. If you do so, we may be unable to continue establishing or administering your trust or, if you are a representative, to continue your appointment or pay commission;
limit the processing of your personal data, including processing that is likely to cause you damage or distress;
request that personal data you provided to us be transmitted to another data user in a structured, commonly used format, where technically feasible; and
opt out of marketing communications at any time.
To exercise any of these rights, write to our Data Protection Officer using the details in Section 15. We may ask you to verify your identity before acting on a request.

title: PERSONAL DATA YOU GIVE US ABOUT OTHER PEOPLE

clauses.text: If you give us personal data about another person, such as a beneficiary, caretaker, witness, joint account holder or settlor, you confirm that you have informed that person of this notice and, where required, obtained their consent for us to process their personal data as described here.
Where that person is below eighteen (18) years of age, the consent of their parent or legal guardian is required.

Identity data, contact data, source of funds, tax residency and bank details are compulsory. If you do not provide them, we will be unable to establish or administer your trust or, if you are a representative, to appoint you or pay you commission. Other information is optional, and we will tell you where that is the case.

The Portal and the Websites use functional cookies and session tokens needed to keep you logged in and to secure your session. We also keep audit logs of actions taken in the Portal for security, compliance and dispute resolution. We do not use third-party advertising cookies.

If a personal data breach occurs that is likely to cause significant harm, we will notify the Personal Data Protection Commissioner and, where required by the PDPA, the affected individuals within the time required by law.

We may update this notice from time to time. The current version, with its effective date, will be posted on the Websites and in the Portal. We will notify you of material changes by email or by notice in the Portal.
Enquiries, complaints and requests under Section 9 may be sent to our Data Protection Officer by email at operation@cnbamanah.com.
